title: Codyssey.dev
problem: Most developer education teaches demos, not how to build and maintain software that lasts.
why: Most developer education teaches demos. I wanted engineers to learn how to build software that survives contact with real users and real time. I set the roadmap, built the product, run it in production, and write the material.
did: Founded and built the platform.
Lead the engineering team, set the roadmap, run production infrastructure, and write the course content.
result: The platform is live and in active development, with courses, learning paths, and articles published.

title: Non-profit fundraising and CRM platform
problem: An all-in-one platform for non-profits needed new fundraising, workflow, and CRM features, and the existing code needed to be more reliable and easier to maintain.
why: Non-profits run on donations and volunteers. Slow releases and fragile features cost them money directly. The Workflows feature I proposed and built let them automate work they were doing by hand.
did: Designed and shipped the new features and the REST APIs behind them.
Refactored existing features.
Cut GitHub Actions build times so the team stopped waiting on CI.
Proposed and got agreement on the architecture (vertical slice architecture, design patterns and principles) and demoed features including the Workflows feature to stakeholders.
Wrote automated tests.
result: Fundraising, workflow, and CRM features shipped to production, backed by tests. GitHub Actions builds that took 30 to 60 minutes now finish in under 10.

did: Designed and shipped features.
